name: Ravi Menon
role: Staff engineer on a platform team of eleven, the person other teams ask 'which tool should we use'.
context: A teammate pasted the link in chat saying 'look at this for our runbooks'. He opens it between two meetings with a keyboard and a screen reader off, but he tabs through everything to test it.
daily_tasks: Reviews designs and incident write-ups, owns the runbooks, evaluates tools for the team, files issues on what breaks. Judges a product by how it fails.
fears: A link that goes nowhere; a form that loses his input; marketing that claims what the page cannot show; being sold to before being told what the thing is.
never_reads: Taglines, testimonials and the footer. He skips any paragraph whose first sentence has no concrete noun.
decides_by: Evidence in the page: a screenshot, a number, a working link. He tabs through the links and notes each dead end, then reads the pricing for limits and the plan boundary. He recommends only what he has seen work.
stake_rules: Primary when the page is about a tool his team could adopt, including its sign-up path. Secondary when the page is about what his team's manager would approve. Bystander on a consumer promotion.
